subject: Benchmark plan & acceptance criteria for AtlasHealth onboarding
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@atlashealth.com>, Ravi Sundaram <ravi@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark plan & acceptance criteria for AtlasHealth onboarding

Hi Laura / Ravi —

Thanks again for the sync yesterday. Attached is a concise benchmark plan wed like to run during onboarding to validate latency and throughput targets for your primary inference flow (clinical note extraction -> summarization). Goal is a clean, evidence-based handoff so Procurement / Eng has confidence in predicted unit costs and latency SLAs.

High-level acceptance targets (proposed):
- Functional correctness: end-to-end output matches provided sample set (pass/fail spot checks)
- P95 latency: <= 280 ms (service time for generation stage)
- P99 latency: <= 900 ms (long-tail allowance; see note below)
- Sustained throughput: 120 req/s for 30 minutes (steady-state)
- Spike handling: 250 req/s for 3 minutes with error rate < 1.0%
- Error rate (overall): < 0.5% during test windows

Planned test phases:
1) Baseline functional tests (sanity, 30m)
2) Ramp tests (15m step ramps to peak)
3) Soak/stability (4 hours at target QPS)
4) Failover validation (simulate region fallback, if applicable)

What we need from AtlasHealth before we run:
- Staging inference endpoint + test key (staging)
- Representative request payloads and response validation rules (JSON samples)
- Expected peak QPS and normal operating profile (hourly breakdown)
- Any IP allowlists or proxy info

Proposed dates: Aug 11 (baseline + ramp) and Aug 12 (soak + evidence handoff). If you prefer we can compress to a single day morning window. Please confirm availability and whether Procurement should be looped in for the acceptance sign-off.

Attachments: atlas_benchmark_plan_v1.xlsx, pretest-checklist.md, slo-evidence-template.csv

Thanks — happy to walk through in a 30-min kickoff.

Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0184

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@atlashealth.com>

Thanks Hannah — this is very clear and appreciated. A few quick asks / clarifications from our side: 

- Can we add a P99.9 (tail) latency sample for the critical route? Were sensitive to extreme tails for certain clinician workflows.
- Please include token/request rate limits in the plan (we have a 5k/min cap on staging tokens).
- Can you confirm the model variant you'll use for the runs (quantized vs fp16) so we can map cost estimates?

Availability: Aug 11 morning (08:00-12:00 PT) works best for our infra team. For the soak run Aug 12 would be fine.

I'll follow up with Procurement to ensure they see the evidence package — cc'ing them on the next thread once dates are locked.

Also: can you include a short section in the evidence pack that maps observed throughput to estimated unit cost (tokens / sec -> $/hour)? That makes approvals faster on our side.

Laura Chen
Head of Platform Integrations | AtlasHealth
laura.chen@atlashealth.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@atlashealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Benchmark plan & acceptance criteria for AtlasHealth onboarding

Laura / Hannah —

Great questions. Quick operational notes from the Test & Onboard team: 

Test harness and phases (what Redwood will run):
- Harness: our internal load runner (bash wrapper + k6 + custom KV-cache probe). We will provide run-harness.sh (attached) and a JSON of request templates.
- Phase 1: Functional baseline: 30 minutes of low qps to verify schema and auth.
- Phase 2: Ramp: 15-minute steps: 5, 20, 50, 100, 150 qps. Collect p50/p90/p95/p99/p99.9 and CPU/GPU utilization per minute.
- Phase 3: Soak: 4 hours at agreed target (120 qps). We will also run a short spike test (250 qps, 3 minutes).
- Phase 4: Evidence capture & handoff: dashboards (Grafana snapshots), raw logs (first/last 5k requests), KV cache hit-rate, model variant info.

Model variant: we will run the official "rwd-infer-v2-quant" variant for primary runs (quantized) and run one short fp16 pass for comparison; details will be captured in the evidence pack.

SLO/evidence mapping (what we will hand over):
- Latency distributions (per-endpoint, per-tenant): p50/p90/p95/p99/p99.9
- Error breakdown (timeouts, 5xx, model errors) with sample ids
- Throughput timeline (1m resolution) + rolling averages
- Resource utilization and kernel metrics (GPU mem, NVLink usage)
- Cost projection: token/sec -> tokens per hour -> estimated $/hour for model + infra (spreadsheet attached)

Pre-test checklist (short):
- Staging endpoint reachable from Redwood (we will validate IPs)
- Test API keys provisioned and rate limits disclosed
- Sample payloads & expected validation rules uploaded to shared Drive
- Whitelist any Redwood egress IPs if needed

Attachments included: run-harness.sh, pretest-checklist.md, atlas_benchmark_plan_v1.xlsx, slo-evidence-template.csv

We can run a quick 20-min tech kickoff tomorrow at 09:00 PT to align on payloads and auth. Hannah, will you schedule?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Onboarding Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Confirming Aug 11 morning for baseline & ramp, Aug 12 for soak is fine. Please include the cost projection sheet in the final evidence pack; Procurement will use that to calibrate reserved capacity pricing.
